collisionDials.commentFinding: Across dial 0-60% (1,000 agents) throughput stayed ~1,100-1,280 tasks/s and land wait p50 ~96-114 s; 0 doubled comments, 0 code changes, nothing lost at any level. Same-declaration collisions resolve at landing ('duplicate, kept the first', or a replay when the declaration is still undocumented) or, with claims on, before any work: at 60% + claims all 8,424 second-of-pair tasks were caught early and 0 duplicates reached the Lander, at ~9% higher throughput (1,276 vs 1,167 tasks/s).

code.note: At dial 0 the losses are model mistakes: 76 of 96 were already wrong in the commit where they landed, 19 were dropped by a later agent that read main with the requirement in; 1 lost in landing (a redo that started before the requirement landed; the redo's start time is approximate). 54 rejected = a harness bug (stale fork read; fixed 16:38), 22 cut by deploys.

Clustering 30% of the tasks did not raise losses (74 vs 96 at dial 0): 66 of 74 were already wrong in the commit where they landed, 53 of them clean merges (the model wrote it wrong), 11 among 229 model replays (~5%, the same rate as fresh work, 53 of 998 clean). 6 dropped by a later agent that read main with the requirement in (4 of them exact by base_sha). 2 lost in landing, both judged by the time rule (their breakers predate base_sha): an upper bound. What clustering cost is time: 145 min vs 40 at dial 0, 238 redos and 229 replays (predicted ~299 replays, 36-61 min: the replays were right, the wall 2.4-4x longer than predicted). glm-4.7 (overflow, 49 tasks) lost 11; Gemini flash-lite 55 of 1,328.

60 lost: 54 wrong when they landed (29 of 743 clean merges, 23 of 468 model replays: 3.9% vs 4.9%), 6 dropped by a later agent (all exact by base_sha), 0 lost in landing. The queue was the wall: 207 min, agents waited p50 1,014 s to land.

code.variant: fast: module lanes + direct Haiku replays
code.note: Same seed, task order, 200 agents and model mix as the baseline (glm took 66 tasks in both, so the mix is equal). 3.9x faster (53 vs 207 min), queue wait p50 7x shorter, 66 more landed, 32 more requirements passing on main. 79 lost: 71 wrong when they landed (35 of 763 clean merges 4.6%, 32 of 481 replays 6.7% vs 4.9% baseline: higher, but 32 vs 23 is within chance at these counts), 8 dropped by a later agent (all by base_sha), 0 lost in landing. The new wall is fetching forks into five lane boxes at once (p50 12.7 s, was 3.3 s).

Same seed, tasks, 200 agents and model mix (glm 66 tasks again). 44.5 min (4.6x faster than the baseline's 207). 66 lost: 57 wrong when they landed (25 of 751 clean merges 3.3%, 28 of 484 replays 5.8%), 9 dropped by a later agent (all by base_sha), 0 lost in landing: the third dial-60 run with 0. Fetch is still p50 13 s: main and the notes ref, not the forks. In this run, change records (git notes) could be missing on main: lanes force-pushed refs/notes/qodebase, and no-op changes had no commit of their own. The code and these counts are unaffected. Fixed in 116d1b7 (notes merged, never force-pushed; lane rebase keeps empty commits) and b3f2b03 (a no-op change lands as its own empty commit), deployed with forq 3cde9b4, and checked on eyal/kata-notes (lanes, 200 tasks): 199 of 199 landed changes have their own commit and their note.

worst.comment:
/**
 * Moves the cursor to the end of the word to the right of the current position using fast navigation.
 * Use it for standard rightward word movement.
 */
worst.why: claims 'fast navigation'; the code uses WordNavigationType.WordEnd (text copied from CursorWordLeft)

worst.comment:
/**
 * Moves the cursor to the end of the word to the right and expands the selection using fast
 * navigation. Use it to select the word to the right.
 */
worst.why: claims 'fast navigation'; the code uses WordNavigationType.WordEnd (copied from CursorWordLeftSelect)

worst.comment:
/**
 * Creates an observable value that informs observers when the value changes. Use this when you need a
 * settable observable with an initial value and an optional name or owner.
 */
worst.why: says the name/owner is optional; this overload takes a required owner (the optional-name form is the other overload)

worst.comment:
/**
 * A command that moves the cursor to the left within a word. Use it to implement leftward word
 * navigation.
 */
worst.why: says it moves 'within a word'; it is the base class for moving left by word boundaries

worst.comment:
/**
 * A command that moves the cursor to the right within a word. Use it to implement rightward word
 * navigation.
 */
worst.why: says it moves 'within a word'; it is the base class for moving right by word boundaries
